data.title: Breadcrumb
data.tagline: Show the path from a broad section to the current page
data.description: Breadcrumbs help people understand where a deeply nested page sits and let them move back to a parent level. They describe location, not browsing history. On shallow sites, a clear title and navigation are often enough.

use: A detail page several levels below the start
avoid: Use it as a record of every page the user visited
Show it on a one-level site
Make the current item look like another link
Replace the main page title with a breadcrumb

lessonPractice.title: Someone is on Projects / Summer campaign / Data report and needs to understand the hierarchy and return to Projects. What should be shown?

options.label: Show 'Projects / Summer campaign / Data report' with linked parent levels
options.feedback: The path communicates the page's stable place in the hierarchy and provides direct navigation to each parent.

options.label: List the last three visited pages in reverse chronological order
options.feedback: Visit history changes with the route taken and does not reliably explain where the current page belongs.

options.label: Show 'Step 3' and mark the previous two pages as completed
options.feedback: These are locations in a hierarchy, not stages of a required process, so completion states are misleading.

data.agentPrompt: Show Projects / Summer campaign / Data report breadcrumbs on the report page. Link parent levels and keep the current page as location text, not visit history. Open the report from different entry points and verify a stable path without narrow-screen overflow.
